purpose: Compact reading guide to existing schemas for the paired R4.3-026 Task/Profile only. Not a new platform schema or validator. Business truth comes only from the mounted scenario. Current R4.3-024/025 execution supersedes historical Protocol/plan/dry-run requirements.

identity_rules: schema_version is exactly r4-0-007-scenario-map/v1; scenario_id is a nonempty string.

topology_decision_ref is a string: empty/whitespace while undecided, otherwise its trimmed value is exactly topology-decision.json. Recording a reference does not create or approve the topology artifact.
All six required_sections are arrays; slices has at least one item, while the other five arrays may be empty. The three inherited sections below are top-level arrays, never fields inside slices[].

rules: An array, possibly empty; no repeated viewpoint per slice; note is nonempty.
Absent viewpoints are unassessed, never implicitly not_applicable. No mandatory seven-phase sequence or one Agent per viewpoint.
Partial expression takes modeled with remaining work/unknowns in note. An expression that correctly preserves necessary unknowns may also be modeled; it does not confirm those facts.

Judge current content, not monotonic status upgrades: when a revision invalidates expression, retain only still-valid scope and identify old references as historical. slices[].status remains a textual overview, not a state machine or percentage.

Note locates the current complete immutable candidate_id/revision/key item_id or approved path, explains analyzed/expressed scope, remaining work/unknowns and next responsible role/input. Note references are semantically checked by Coordinator, not a new structured field or regex gate.

definition_id is a stable neutral semantic key, not an IRI; it is unique within the scenario/authorized Project. Same term with different meaning_scope may have distinct keys. Do not merge unconfirmed synonyms.
owner_slice is an existing slices[].slice_id, and used_by_slices contains existing slice IDs; maintenance ownership grants no semantic access.
candidate_refs may be empty before publication; otherwise each points to an item in a complete immutable unified candidate at its current revision.
Same definition across candidates reuses the approved read/receipt-bound platform identity; never create a synonymous duplicate. confirmed means business confirmation only.
Each item is an object with exactly these fields. from_slice and to_slice are existing slices[].slice_id values.
direction is a nonempty string, with no structural enum. connection_points is a nonempty array of nonempty strings.
Record actual dependencies from authorized inputs and explain their direction; example values illustrate syntax only and prescribe no business dependency.
Each item is an object with exactly these fields. question_id and question are nonempty strings.
spans_slices is an array with at least two entries, each an existing slices[].slice_id value. Structural validation does not impose a uniqueness check.
Use authorized public questions only; this section is not approval and must not contain hidden acceptance questions or expected answers.
Each item is an object with exactly these fields; all three values are nonempty strings. status has no structural enum.
Record actual unresolved topics and who or what is needed to resolve them; do not invent missing business facts.

adjustments.rule: Nonempty strings. Use [] when no substantive change; this fresh bounded task does not require shared-definition change review.

rules: Closed top-level keys: schema_version, scenario_id, topology_decision_ref and the six required_sections. All sections are arrays; slices is nonempty. Contract metadata is not artifact content.

Slices use nonempty strings and unique slice_id; viewpoints is an array and may be empty. No mandatory view count or sequence. Shared terms may be empty when no cross-slice reuse; otherwise keep a unique definition_id and a known owner_slice.

Cross-slice questions only use actual public projection entries spanning at least two actual slices. With no cross-slice scope use [], retain that limited coverage; do not invent a second slice or wider acceptance.

Coordinator alone writes scenario-map/scenario-map.json and scenario-map/topology-decision.json. Before terminal, check current candidate content and update locatable progress in notes; a bound handoff map is never overwritten later.
at least three options and always the three required option_ids; custom options may be appended

each options entry has exactly the two option_fields: option_id is a non-empty string, and assessment is an object whose keys are exactly the six dimensions listed above, each with a non-empty value; the dimensions are assessment keys, never an option-level dimensions container (a wrong option shape is reported as topology_schema_mismatch)

every option assesses all six dimensions with non-empty values; the dimensions are concept cohesion, relation density, reuse, permission boundary, change cadence, and cross-domain query, never table count or team count
selecting single_ontology does not waive the comparison: the full three-option, six-dimension record is still required
selected_option must be one of the listed options and rationale must be non-empty

R4.0-029 existing topology: entries are mutually exclusive {ontology_id, slice_ids} for explicit authorized existing IDs or {name, slice_ids} for new creation. New entries require allow_new_ontologies and current business topology approval; do not adopt same-name resources or precreate a first Ontology. A single_ontology selection may supply exactly one existing-ID entry. Original create topology keeps its name-based at-least-two plan contract. Each slice must be covered; slices may overlap.

For fresh create scope, omit ontology_plan when selected_option=single_ontology; every other selection requires a name-based plan with at least two entries covering all actual slices. Existing-ID scope follows its explicit authorized binding rules above.
create/name-only plans require at least two; an existing-ID single_ontology plan may contain one
name or ontology_id values are non-empty and unique within the plan
slice_ids is a non-empty list of distinct slice_ids of the current scenario map
every scenario-map slice belongs to at least one planned Ontology; a slice may be served by more than one planned Ontology
existing mode supports explicit ID entries and a single existing-ID entry for single_ontology; create/new-name entries still require authorization and receipt reconciliation

Publish under stage3-neutral-graph/candidates/<candidate_id>-r<revision>.json. schema_version and all listed fields are required; each item has item_fields plus only supported item_optional_fields. revision is an integer >=1, item_id is unique and neutral; scenario_id/candidate_id are nonempty strings. New revisions are complete and immutable.

items is a nonempty array. business_meaning is a string, unknowns and explicit_unknowns are string arrays. slice_ids is a nonempty string array of actual scope IDs. shared_scope is null/empty except a scoped commonality relation. relation_endpoints is null for non-relations and {from_item_id,to_item_id} for relations.

Use the mounted direct-modeling contract for value rules and definition_ref/existing_resource_ref. Fields are semantic, never command envelopes or guessed platform identities. Business meaning and item unknowns become supported semantic_definition fields; semantic_definition uses business_meaning/unknowns when needed.

For this Task entity/property/relation suffice to express the business scope; other registered kinds are not an invitation to add mappings or metrics. A predicate definition may be a separate technical item; do not infer business scope or Ontology topology from item count.

Relations do not accept semantic_definition. Preserve meaningful relationship text and unknowns on the predicate definition or supported ordinary definition resources. For a relation the business_meaning must agree with its predicate definition; keep relation item unknowns empty if its required semantics are already expressed on that definition.
No stage3 slot, translation approval, dry-run proof or Protocol handshake is a prerequisite to direct submission. Coordinator retains necessary source/scope/topology decisions in its existing notes.

handoff: Modeling submits directly, keeps actual application/read/association-check references and closes owned resources. Coordinator synchronizes current map and reports after Modeling. Host seals production and releases CQ, then starts existing independent read-only Consumer/Judge acceptance; no production evidence generation or repair during acceptance.
